correctness.rationale: For two clients, the FedSplit reflected point \(2x-z_j\) is exactly the other client state. The scalar quadratic proximal map is affine with reflection coefficient \(r_j=(1-sa_j)/(1+sa_j)\), giving the exact error matrix \(\begin{bmatrix}0&r_1\\r_2&0\end{bmatrix}\). Its square is \(r_1r_2I\), so the spectral radius and the two-round nilpotency at \(s=1/a_j\) are exact. Direct package replay checks the formulas and fixed-point average independently.

value.rationale: The finding gives an exact communication-complexity collapse, not merely a slightly better contraction constant. It shows that heterogeneity can be exploited constructively: matching the proximal parameter to either one client's curvature annihilates one reflection and the two-client cross-coupling annihilates the remaining state one round later. This supplies a sharp instancewise benchmark for federated splitting and clarifies a phenomenon hidden by worst-case condition-number rate bounds.
